reserveReview.rationale: 2026-09-29 review: the SBI Shinsei Trust / SBI VC Trade press release of 2026-09-07 (PDF and HTML both retrieved) states that, using the amended Payment Services Act framework in force since 2026-06-01, ¥10.0 billion of the trust property backing JPYSC is now invested in short-term JGBs (residual maturity capped at 3 months under the framework, i.e. a stated hard maximum of 90 days), and that JPYSC issuance stood at approximately ¥20.1 billion (約201億円) as of 2026-09-07. The composition is therefore ¥10.0B short-term JGBs (10.0/20.1 = 49.8%) and approximately ¥10.1B yen demand deposits (50.2%); the deposit leg is derived as issuance minus the stated JGB amount under the 1:1 trust structure — the release does not separately state a deposit amount — and the pre-existing arrangement is corroborated by the trustee's statutory disclosure as of 2026-06-30 (deposits ¥10,008,304,794 against issuance ¥10,008,294,794, no JGB line). The release also reports ≈¥6.9B of JPYSC Lending applications, which is demand on top of the ¥20.1B issuance and is not part of today's backing. The statutory disclosure page itself remains unreachable outside Japan (fetch attempts on 2026-09-29 timed out), so the press release is the newest retrievable dated composition; no independent attestation program exists. The JGB slice keeps a conservative seven-day liquidity horizon (settlement of ≤3-month JGBs ahead of redemption) rather than an unstated faster assumption; deposit liquidity remains immediate.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Issuer press release dated 2026-09-07 (JPYSC trust property: ¥10.0B short-term JGBs against ≈¥20.1B issuance, remainder demand deposits under the pre-existing arrangement confirmed by the trustee statutory disclosure as of 2026-06-30); amended PSA trust-type rules cap JGB/time-deposit allocation at 50% of issuance with ≤3-month residual maturity.
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: Both buckets of the 1:1 trust property are classified — the JGB bucket from the issuer-stated ¥10.0B and the deposit bucket as the derived residual (issuance minus the stated JGB amount, not separately issuer-stated) — so no notional is unclassified at the asset-class level. Residual unknowns: the issuance figure is stated as approximate (約201億円), exact deposit balances and their banks are not published, JGB issue numbers and weighted maturity are not disclosed, the release does not state whether any principal-protected time deposits (also permitted up to the 50% cap) are held, and the trustee may rebalance up to the 50% cap without granular disclosure. The trustee's statutory disclosure page is geo-restricted and there is no third-party attestation; only FSA-supervised trustee disclosure exists.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: 2026-09-29: JPYSC is a trust-type Type III Electronic Payment Instrument; SBI Shinsei Trust Bank, as issuer-trustee, holds the backing assets as trust property segregated from its own assets under the FSA framework, with SBI VC Trade as issuing entity giving investment instructions. The underlying deposit banks for the yen demand-deposit portion and the custody venue of the JGB positions are not disclosed, and no rehypothecation terms are published; shares between custodial arrangements are therefore omitted rather than estimated.
